next.reason: §1985:IV.4.2.2.1 SR1 (the paragraph as Amendment 2, X3.23b-1993, replaced it; Errata C198): "For all COBOL words excluding the words LENGTH, RANDOM, and SUM: a. Reserved words form disjoint sets with user-defined words, system-names, and function-names. b. ... The same COBOL word may be used as a function-name, as a system-name, and as a user-defined word." 2023 keeps (a) against user-defined words and system-names, §2023:8.3.2.1 SR1 "Reserved words shall not be used as user-defined words or system-names", and (b) between system-names and user-defined words, §2023:8.3.2.1 SR4 "A given word may be used as a system-name and as a user-defined word". The function-name part has a different requirement, §2023:8.3.2.1 SR5: "Intrinsic-function-names may be used as user-defined words and system-names, except for — intrinsic function names LENGTH, RANDOM, SIGN, and SUM; and — intrinsic function names identified in a function-specifier in the REPOSITORY paragraph." The words that differ: "SIGN", a fourth word that is both reserved (§2023:8.9) and an intrinsic function name (§2023:8.11), where 1985 excludes three; and the added case "identified in a function-specifier in the REPOSITORY paragraph", in which a function-name may NOT be a user-defined word or a system-name, where 1985 lets every function-name outside the three be one. 2023 has no rule of its own for the 1985 sentence that context determines the classification.
